title: [C17T2] Police Budget 2017-2018
prompt: The table and charts below give information on the police budget for 2017 and 2018 in one area of Britain. The table shows where the money came from and the charts show how it was distributed. Summarize the information and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table and pie charts illustrate the police budget in terms of funding sources and spending allocation in one area of Britain for 2017 and 2018.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the police budget experienced growth across all funding sources between the two years. In terms of expenditure, there was a notable shift towards increased technology spending, while the proportion allocated to buildings and transport declined accordingly.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding funding sources, the national government was the largest contributor in 2017 at £175.5 million, significantly higher than local taxes which provided £91.2 million, while other sources contributed £38 million. By 2018, local taxes showed the most substantial increase, rising by £11.1 million to £102.3 million. The national government funding also grew, though more modestly, to £177.8 million, while other sources increased marginally to £38.5 million.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for spending allocation, the proportion of spending on buildings and transport dominated the budget in 2017, accounting for three-quarters of expenditure at 75%, while that figure for salary costs for officers and staff represented 17%, and technology constituted only 8%. However, technology spending nearly doubled its share to 14% in 2018, while that of buildings and transport decreased to 69%. Meanwhile, salary costs remained stable at 17% throughout the period.
